notes: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at AUC (Spring 2027 cohort) is an institution-wide graduate fellowship: AUC's Fellowships Listings state it is open to African applicants 'admitted to any field of graduate studies at AUC', so no professor is attached to the scholarship itself. Programme inquiries: mastercardfdn@aucegypt.edu (programme office, not a supervisor). The three faculty above are verified from official aucegypt.edu profile pages in graduate programs aligned with the fellowship's stated mission of 'fields that promote African economic development' (economics, public policy, labour/social policy); relationship_type is program_relevant_faculty, not scholarship-named supervisors. Their institutional emails were published on those profile pages and are marked verified.

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda (2026/2027 Cohort 5) is a 10-year university-wide scholarship covering primarily undergraduate study (site states 'Among 1,200 scholars, 90% will be undergraduates', 'Ten percent of the Scholars will be admitted to the Master's program'). Official pages checked: https://mcfsp.ur.ac.rw/ (programme site) and https://mcfsprecruitment.ur.ac.rw (application portal) - both accessible; no supervising professors or faculty contacts are named on either. Programme contact is an office, not a professor: mcfsp@ur.ac.rw. Undergraduate scholarships have no supervising professor, and no supervisor names appear on the official programme pages.

The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship is a central government scheme of the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs administered by Campus France. Per the official page, 'Applications are submitted exclusively by French higher education institutions' and 'Applications sent directly by students or by foreign institutions will be declared ineligible' - there is no attached institution or professor; the host institution submits the file after admitting the student, so no supervising faculty can be verified for the scholarship itself.

Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (ESKAS) are awarded centrally by the Swiss Confederation via the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS). The official SERI page states: 'Prerequisite: the scholarship application must be backed by an academic supervisor in Switzerland who is willing to direct and guide the applicant's proposed research' - i.e. applicants must individually secure a supervisor at a Swiss institution; no professor is attached to the scholarship.

DAAD Study Scholarships for STEM Disciplines is a German Federal Foreign Office-funded national scheme administered through the DAAD scholarship database. The official page confirms it funds 'a complete Master's degree (full-time, on-campus) at a state or state-recognised university in Germany' chosen by the applicant, with no attached institution or professor; applications go through the central DAAD portal.

The Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships program is a federal tri-agency scholarship (CIHR, NSERC, SSHRC). Per vanier.gc.ca, 'Candidates must be nominated by a Canadian institution with a quota to host Vanier scholars' - a central national competition with no attached professor. (The site also notes applications are no longer accepted, superseded by the Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Doctoral program.)
